faqs.q: What is a fillable PDF form?

faqs.q: Why does my PDF show no fields?

faqs.q: Can I edit the answers after downloading?

fill-pdf-form.formula:
pages_needed = ceil(total_fields / 8)

At the default layout each A4 page fits 8 fields (76 pt spacing, 660 pt of usable height).
howTo: Choose a mode: Fill an existing form, or Create a new fillable PDF.
To fill: upload your PDF. The tool lists every detected field with its name and type.
Enter your answers — type into text fields, tick checkboxes, pick dropdown options.
Click the fill button to bake your answers into the file and download the completed PDF.
To create: add rows for each field you need, pick text, checkbox or dropdown, name them, then build and download your new fillable PDF.
keyFacts: A fillable PDF uses the AcroForm standard: interactive field objects stored inside the PDF file itself, not just drawn text.
This tool auto-detects five field kinds: text fields, checkboxes, dropdowns, radio groups and option lists.
After filling, field appearance streams are regenerated so your answers show correctly in Adobe Reader, browsers and mobile viewers.
In Create mode each A4 page holds up to 8 fields at the default 76-point spacing before a new page starts.
Everything runs locally with the pdf-lib engine — files are never uploaded anywhere. The practical limit is 50 MB per file.

limitations: XFA (XML Forms Architecture) forms are not supported — only classic AcroForm fields are detected.
Password-protected PDFs may fail to parse unless the password is removed first.
This tool fills form fields; it cannot add or remove digital signatures or flatten scanned images into fields.
Field appearances are regenerated generically, so fonts may look slightly different from the original authoring software.

fill-pdf-form.workedExample:
You design a job application form with 20 fields.
Usable height per A4 page: 790 - 130 = 660 pt.
Fields per page: floor(660 / 76) = 8.
Pages needed: ceil(20 / 8) = ceil(2.5) = 3 pages.
The tool generates a 3-page PDF: 8 fields on page 1, 8 on page 2, 4 on page 3.
